newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian wine gets "appellation controlee" status.
newsitem.headline: Belgian wine gets "appellation controlee" status.

text.p: Belgium's wine makers are celebrating official permission to put an "appellation controlee" quality label on their bottles.

A decree granting the 10 Hagelandse Wijnbouwers (Hageland Winegrowers) from near Leuven in central Belgium their label, or Hagelandse wijn Gecontroleerde Oorsprongsbenaming, was signed by the Flanders regional government on Thursday.

"The consumer can now be sure that the wine he is drinking is from Hageland and that it conforms with quality standards laid down in law," Maurice Fol, the chairman of the local wine producers' association, told Reuters.
It seems, however, that the wine growers victory in this country better known for its beer has yet to reach official circles.
Asked if French President Jacques Chirac was offered Belgian wine during a dinner at Belgium's royal palace on Wednesday, a palace spokeswoman said, "I think not. It was French."
